cases.sentence: Когда ___ шли со своими сотнями и тысячами воинов, Давид и его люди шли сзади с Ахишем.
cases.explain: «филистимские правители» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds and by thousands; and David and his men passed on in the rear with Achish.

cases.sentence: Но ___ разгневались на него и сказали:
cases.explain: «филистимские начальники» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him; and the princes of the Philistines said to him, “Make the man return, that he may go back to his place where you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. For with what should this fellow reconcile himself to his lord? Should it not be with the heads of these men?

cases.sentence: Поворачивай и иди с миром; не делай ничего, что могло бы рассердить ___.
cases.explain: «филистимских правителей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Therefore now return, and go in peace, that you not displease the lords of the Philistines.”

cases.sentence: − Но что же я сделал? − спросил Давид. − Что плохого ты нашел в твоем слуге с того дня, когда я пришел к тебе, и до ___?
cases.explain: «сегодняшнего дня» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: David said to Achish, “But what have I done? What have you found in your servant so long as I have been before you to this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
